text: {"claims":[{"cid":"c1","text":"Time restricted eating lowered daily energy intake and produced weight loss over twelve weeks.","cited_pids":["fasting#0"]},{"cid":"c2","text":"An eating window rule was reported to be easier to adhere to than continuous calorie restriction.","cited_pids":["fasting#1","fasting#3"]},{"cid":"c3","text":"Reduced evening snacking accounted for a meaningful share of the energy deficit in time restricted eating.","cited_pids":["fasting#1","fasting#3"]},{"cid":"c4","text":"Head-to-head trials that matched total calories found no weight loss advantage of intermittent fasting over continuous calorie restriction across twelve months.","cited_pids":["fasting#4"]},{"cid":"c5","text":"Several studies report higher dropout rates in intermittent fasting arms than in continuous restriction arms.","cited_pids":["fasting#6"]},{"cid":"c6","text":"In one short trial, the benefits of intermittent fasting largely disappeared once energy intake was controlled.","cited_pids":["fasting#7"]},{"cid":"c7","text":"A trial reported greater lean mass loss in the intermittent fasting arm.","cited_pids":["fasting#5"]},{"cid":"c8","text":"Intermittent fasting appears effective mainly as a route to a calorie deficit, and its unique advantage beyond calorie reduction is unproven.","cited_pids":[]}]}
